chapter: Billie Holiday, Basie leadership and studio work
title: Film work: Westerns, Indian parts and being in-between
summary: He worked on Westerns, played Indians and rode an elephant, owing to his light complexion.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Do you remember any particular films

Well, I worked with all of the stars and things in those days. I worked with Hepburn, Richard Barthelmus, (PHONETIC), these are all people that you wouldn't really know about. Back with -- oh, gee. I never was much for names, but I worked with so many people. I just -- they all just run together in my head. I was never a person to actually remember too much about pictures, because I had seen so many of them made in person that there was no fantasy in my mind about how a picture should be made because I knew that there was all front and no foundation and it was all a front board and no back behind it.

I worked in Westerns, all of those sort of things in those days, whatever there was to do, I worked at them. As a matter of fact, I even rode a few horses and things in Westerns when I was a young kid.

On camera. I was, by me being a little light-complected, I couldn't get jobs being a black guy, so I got a few jobs putting some things around my head and being an Indian in a scene or something. I even rode a elephant once with a turban.
Oh, no, I don't know what picture. This is way back.
It would be fun to look for you on the late show.
Well, run across one every once in a while. You see, I was always a in-betweener. I was too light to be black and I was too black to be white. So, I was in what you might call a chickenshit position.
So you made the best of it?
Yeah. Oh, definitely. Intelligence wins out over all.
